title: Flag Fen unveils spooky Halloween events including ghost hunts and Fright Night
excerpt: Flag Fen Archaeology Park is gearing up for Halloween with a range of immersive events.
content:
Flag Fen Archaeology Park is gearing up for Halloween with a range of immersive events.

The spooky line-up includes ghost hunting, Halloween adventures, and an evening of mediumship.

The fun starts with a Paranormal Evening on Saturday, October 3, allowing visitors to explore the ancient site after dark with professional ghost hunters, Spirit Norwich.

The evening will feature tales of Flag Fen's prehistoric past from storyteller Michelle Bullivant, followed by a paranormal investigation using various equipment.

Paranormal evening (Image: Flag Fen)

From October 24 to 31, families can enjoy Halloween Fun, transforming Flag Fen into an autumn adventure for the school half-term.

Activities include pumpkin picking, broomstick making, a Fairytale Scarecrow Trail, and a search for missing spell pages in the roundhouse.

There will also be opportunities to toast marshmallows around the fire.

An Evening of Mediumship with Nicola Ghigi is scheduled for Friday, October 23.

The 90-minute event features two sessions, with the Roundhouse Café open for refreshments.

Flag Fen's Halloween festivities conclude with Fright Night on Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31.

The landscape will take on a darker atmosphere, with themed zones inspired by ancient history and East Anglian folklore.

The experience, created in collaboration with Kindred Drama, will include theatrical encounters, storytelling, and haunting visuals.

Pumpkin patch (Image: Flag Fen)

On Saturday, October 24, the park hosts its next Astronomy Evening, inviting visitors to explore the night sky guided by astronomer Dean Watson.

Visitors can also view Fen to Fire, an immersive digital art installation reconstructing the 3,000-year-old Must Farm settlement, until October 18.

The free installation uses 3D modelling, motion capture, and AI to offer a glimpse into life at the remarkable Bronze Age settlement near Whittlesey.

With a mix of ancient history, autumn adventures, and spooky encounters, October is set to be a busy month at Flag Fen.

For more information, including booking details, visit flagfen.org.uk/events.
